prompt_name: Optimize FastPrep deviation report and remove AI-generated code noise
scope: Existing data_prep_tool repository after successful V4 report generation
prompt:
You are GitHub Copilot Chat working inside the existing data_prep_tool repository. Perform a tightly scoped cleanup and optimization pass on the already working Compare Against Standard V4 feature.

DO NOT rewrite the application. DO NOT change the Train Type / IMU generator behavior. DO NOT remove the current successful ability to create Workbook_Deviations.xlsx. DO NOT modify either source .xlsm workbook. DO NOT invent new sheets, rules, parameters, or domain assumptions.

This task is based on measured output from a real generated report and direct code review. Implement exactly the changes below.

MEASURED CURRENT REPORT FACTS
The generated Workbook_Deviations.xlsx is valid and has the correct seven headers:
Change No, Sheet, Cell, Standard Value, Project Value, Parameter, Rule.

Measured report statistics:
- 6,621 deviation rows
- 36 sheets represented
- only 216 rows have Parameter and Rule
- Passive Rules coverage is 3.26%
- 5,824 rows have Standard Value blank or "-"
- largest contributors:
  - MVB.ProcessData: 2,630 rows
  - test IO_to_monitor: 587 rows
  - Train type: 578 rows
  - IO_listing: 395 rows
  - Test Binary Outputs: 378 rows
  - Test Binary Inputs: 353 rows
  - Communication config.: 304 rows
  - System_interface_description: 246 rows
  - Project: 163 rows
  - Test Generic Inputs_ERTMS: 163 rows
- IO_listing row 82 alone produces 256 cell differences.

Interpretation that must guide implementation:
- The comparator is technically finding differences, but the main report is dominated by structural/population differences where Standard contains blank or "-" and Project contains a value.
- Those differences must NOT be silently discarded because some may be important.
- The main user-facing sheet should be concise and actionable.
- The complete raw differences must remain available on a separate worksheet.
- Test* sheets must NOT be globally excluded because real Passive Rules reference Test sheets.
- Technical sheets must not be blindly hardcoded out of comparison. Use metadata-driven behavior.

TARGET REPORT DESIGN
Keep the existing output workbook and exact seven-column schema. Create three worksheets:

1. "List of Project Deviations"
   Main actionable report. Exact columns:
   Change No, Sheet, Cell, Standard Value, Project Value, Parameter, Rule

   Include a deviation if ANY condition is true:
   - Parameter is non-empty, OR
   - Rule is non-empty, OR
   - Standard Value is not a placeholder.

   Placeholder definition for this filtering only:
   - None
   - empty string after trimming
   - "-" after trimming

   Do not treat 0, False, "0", "NO", "FALSE", or "ERROR" as placeholders.
   Do not modify the underlying comparison normalization.

2. "All Cell Differences"
   Complete raw list of all deviations currently produced, including standard blank/"-" to project value differences. Exact same seven columns.
   This worksheet guarantees no data loss.

3. "Summary"
   A compact summary containing:
   - Standard display name
   - Standard workbook filename
   - Project workbook filename if available in result/context
   - comparison execution time
   - total sheets compared
   - total cells compared
   - total raw differences
   - actionable differences count
   - Passive Rules enriched differences count
   - differences grouped by sheet, descending count
   - a note explaining that All Cell Differences contains complete raw output

Do not add columns to the two deviation sheets.

REPORT GENERATOR CHANGES
Modify app/comparison/report_generator.py minimally:
- Keep ReportGenerator public API compatible.
- Add small private helpers instead of duplicating formatting logic:
  - _is_placeholder(value)
  - _is_actionable(deviation)
  - _write_deviation_sheet(workbook, title, deviations)
  - _apply_sheet_formatting(worksheet)
  - _write_summary_sheet(...)
- Use the same natural cell sorting already present.
- Renumber Change No independently on each deviation sheet starting from 1.
- Freeze panes A2 and apply auto-filter on both deviation sheets.
- Reuse one NamedStyle or shared style objects rather than recreating style objects per cell.
- Keep widths A=12, B=28, C=12, D=28, E=28, F=32, G=22.
- Wrap text in D:G.
- Set vertical alignment to top.
- Ensure worksheet title length is legal.
- Maintain .xlsx output.
- Never save source workbooks.

MODELS / RESULT CONTEXT
Do not add unnecessary generic abstractions. If Summary needs filenames, minimally extend WorkbookComparisonResult with optional fields:
- standard_workbook_file: str = ""
- project_workbook_file: str = ""
Populate them in WorkbookComparator using os.path.basename/pathlib.Path.name.
Keep backward compatibility with existing tests by using defaults.

PASSIVE RULES PARSER CODE REVIEW FIXES
Review app/comparison/passive_rules_parser.py and implement these exact corrections:
1. Respect metadata passive_rules.enabled. If false, build_map returns {} immediately.
2. Clear self._sheet_indexes at the start of build_map so indexes from one workbook cannot leak into another workbook if parser instance is reused.
3. Remove unused imports. In the reviewed version column_index_from_string was imported but unused.
4. Replace broad exception handling in _safe_int with only TypeError and ValueError.
5. Continue fault tolerance for an individual bad Passive Rules row, but aggregate diagnostics instead of logging hundreds of warning lines.
6. Track counts:
   - parsed rows
   - mapped rows
   - skipped missing sheet
   - skipped invalid offsets
   - skipped missing anchor
   - skipped invalid target
7. Log one INFO summary after parsing and only DEBUG details for individual expected mapping misses. Unexpected exceptions may remain WARNING with row number.
8. Deduplicate PassiveRuleMatch entries for the same target cell while preserving first-seen order.
9. Do not fuzzy match.
10. Do not lowercase values. Exact match after whitespace/newline normalization remains required.
11. Keep lazy per-sheet indexing.
12. Add a safe cap based on the Passive Rules worksheet dimensions, but do not hardcode a final row.

PASSIVE RULES DIAGNOSTICS
Expose a small immutable diagnostics dataclass or a read-only property only if needed by tests/report summary. Do not add diagnostics columns to the deviation report. At minimum, log the parser summary.

WORKBOOK COMPARATOR OPTIMIZATION
Review app/comparison/workbook_comparator.py and implement only evidence-based optimizations:
1. Keep data_only=True, read_only=True, keep_vba=True.
2. Keep exact value comparison and preservation of numeric-looking strings such as "00000004".
3. Do not introduce semantic conversion between 4 and "00000004". They remain different.
4. Build Passive Rules map once per comparison.
5. Build a set of passive map keys for O(1) lookup.
6. Avoid repeatedly reading metadata properties inside inner cell loops. Cache local references before iterating.
7. Use iter_rows(values_only=True) for value comparison where practical, but retain coordinates deterministically by computing row/column coordinates. Do not instantiate or mutate cells in read-only worksheets.
8. Keep union-of-used-ranges behavior.
9. Add a sanity guard for pathological worksheet dimensions. If dimension area is unexpectedly huge, log the sheet name/dimensions and continue using a safe strategy based on populated rows. Do not silently skip real data.
10. Close both workbooks in a finally block.
11. Preserve the original exception as chained cause using `raise ... from exc`.
12. Do not catch bare Exception around the entire comparison unless it is re-raised with precise context.
13. Do not add multiprocessing. openpyxl workbook objects are not safe/useful for that here.
14. Do not add pandas.

SHEET SELECTION
Keep metadata-driven visible-minus-blacklist comparison.
Do not globally ignore Test* sheets.
Do not automatically ignore MVB.ProcessData or IO_listing, because the complete raw report must retain these changes.

Instead, add optional metadata configuration under compare:
"actionable_report": {
  "exclude_sheets": [],
  "exclude_prefixes": [],
  "include_mapped_even_if_excluded": true,
  "placeholder_values": [null, "", "-"]
}

Rules:
- This configuration affects only "List of Project Deviations".
- It never affects "All Cell Differences".
- Default exclude lists must be empty.
- If a mapped deviation has Parameter or Rule and include_mapped_even_if_excluded is true, keep it in the actionable sheet.
- Do not inject project-specific sheet exclusions without an explicit metadata entry.

REPORT QUALITY ISSUES TO PRESERVE/VERIFY
- Some rows are correctly enriched, for example Communication config. and Dynamic train data set entries.
- Most technical block differences are unmapped. This is expected and must not be misrepresented as parser failure without diagnostics.
- Standard "-" to Project value rows are real raw differences but should normally live only in All Cell Differences unless mapped.
- Existing seven-column order is correct and must not change.

REPOSITORY CLEANUP AND AI-HALLUCINATION REVIEW
Perform a direct repository review, not speculative cleanup.

Required fixes:
1. requirements.txt must use valid pinned syntax:
   openpyxl==3.1.5
   pyinstaller==6.21.0
   msoffcrypto-tool==6.0.0
2. Remove unused imports in files you touch.
3. Remove duplicate helper methods only when behavior is identical and tests cover the replacement.
4. Do not remove train_type_values.json or excel_mapping.json if still used by legacy services/tests.
5. Do not remove SharePoint repository code as part of this task.
6. Keep scalak.py as a developer helper if complete.
7. Ensure repo_after_*.txt, logs, build, dist, caches are ignored.
8. Do not commit generated Workbook_Deviations.xlsx unless explicitly intended as a test fixture.
9. Do not leave old Copilot prompt JSON files in runtime paths. If retained for documentation, move them to docs/prompts/ and make sure application code never imports them.
10. Correct README layering documentation. Current UI directly imports app.comparison modules, so either:
    - accurately document that ui may depend on comparison, OR
    - introduce a service facade only if it clearly reduces coupling without unnecessary code.
    Prefer the documentation correction for this task.
11. Keep the embedded standard metadata loader with utf-8-sig and precise path errors.
12. Do not move the standard workbook unless config/runtime asset paths are updated and tested.
13. Do not log the workbook password.
14. Do not add comments that restate obvious code line by line.
15. Remove vague comments like "for future use" unless linked to actual behavior.
16. Avoid one-line wrapper functions that add no validation, logging, or abstraction value.

README UPDATE
Update comparison documentation to explain:
- Main sheet shows actionable differences.
- All Cell Differences contains complete raw differences.
- Summary gives counts by sheet.
- Placeholder differences are not deleted, only separated.
- Project workbook must be recalculated and saved in Excel first.

TESTS
Add/adjust deterministic unit tests:
1. Report has exactly three sheets in this order:
   Summary
   List of Project Deviations
   All Cell Differences
2. Both deviation sheets have exact seven headers.
3. A deviation with Standard Value "-" and no mapping appears only in All Cell Differences.
4. A deviation with Standard Value "-" but Parameter/Rule populated appears in both deviation sheets.
5. A deviation with Standard Value 0 and Project Value 1 appears in both sheets.
6. Raw sheet row count equals all result deviations.
7. Actionable sheet row count follows exact rule above.
8. Summary counts match workbook result.
9. PassiveRulesParser returns {} when disabled.
10. Parser cache is reset between workbook instances.
11. Duplicate PassiveRuleMatch entries are deduplicated preserving order.
12. Comparator still detects missing sheets and changed cells.
13. Metadata actionable_report exclusions affect only main sheet, never raw sheet.
14. Existing Train Type / Rebuild tests still pass.

Do not use the real FastPrep workbook in unit tests. Use tiny temporary workbooks.

VALIDATION
Run exactly:
python -m compileall .
python -m unittest discover -s tests

Then manually generate a report using the same real project workbook and verify:
- All Cell Differences still contains 6,621 rows for the same unchanged inputs, unless a genuine comparator bug was fixed and documented.
- List of Project Deviations is substantially smaller.
- No raw differences are lost.
- Parameter and Rule values remain present for mapped rows.
- Summary sheet counts reconcile exactly.

DELIVERABLE
Make the code changes and provide a concise final summary listing:
- files changed
- tests added/changed
- compile result
- test result
- any measured change to report row counts

Do not propose optional rewrites. Do not stop at analysis. Implement the exact scoped changes above.
